beads.english: Let there be a drachm of chalcitis; of the grape, when two parts are left, having pressed it out, and having ground myrrh and saffron, mix in the must, boil it in the sun, and with this anoint those suffering violent pains; let it be kept in a copper [917] vessel.

beads.greek: ὑπὸ ὑστερικῶν πνιγομένων γνῶσις· πιέσαι τοῖσι δυσὶ δακτύλοισι καὶ ἢν αἴσθηται, τὰ ὑστερικά ἐστιν, ἢν δὲ μὴ, σπασμώδεα.
beads.english: Diagnosis of women suffocated by uterine affections: press with the two fingers, and if she feels it, the condition is uterine; if not, it is convulsive.

beads.greek: τοῖσιν ὑδρωπιώδεσιν. μηκώνειον λεκίσκιον Ἀττικὸν στρογγύλον πόσις.
beads.english: For those in a dropsical state: of mēkōneion, a round Attic lekiskion is the draught.

beads.greek: λεπίδος μηλαὶ τρεῖς τῷ πλάτει καὶ ἀλεύρου σητανίου, κολλήσαντα ταῦτα, λεῖα τρίψας, καταποτὰ ξυστρέψας, δίδου· κάτω ὕδωρ καθαίρει καὶ κοιλίην ἐκκοπροῖ.
beads.english: Of scale, three probes' breadth, and of sētanion flour; having glued these together, ground them fine and rolled them into pills, give them; it purges water downwards and empties the bowel of faeces.

beads.greek: ἐς ἰσχάδας, ὀποῦ τοῦ τιθυμάλλου ἀπόσταζε ὁκόσον ἑπτάκις ἐς ἑκάστην τῷ εἰρημένῳ, εἶτα ἐς καινὸν ἄγγος συνθεὶς ταμιεύεσθαι, δίδου τῷ εἰρημένῳ πρὸ τῶν σιτίων.
beads.english: Onto dried figs drip juice of tithymallos, about seven times onto each, with the aforesaid; then, putting them together into a new vessel, store them, and give them to the aforesaid patient before food.

beads.greek: τοῖς ὑδρωπικοῖς τὸ μὲν κώνιον τρίβων, ὕδωρ ἐπιχέας, δίδου ἐσθίειν καὶ ἐπιπίνειν.
beads.english: To the dropsical, grind the kōnion, pour water over it, and give it to eat and to drink after.

beads.greek: καὶ τὸ μηκώνειον τρίβων, ὕδωρ ἐπιχέων καὶ διηθέων, ἄλευρον φύρων, ἴτριον ὀπτῶν, μέλι ἑφθὸν παραχέων, τοῖσιν ὑδρωπικοῖσι τρώγειν δίδου, καὶ ἐπιπίνειν γλυκὺν ὑδαρέα, ἢ μελίκρητον ὑδαρές.
beads.english: And grinding the mēkōneion, pouring water over it and straining it, kneading flour, baking a sesame cake, pouring boiled honey over it, give it to the dropsical to chew, and to drink after it sweet wine diluted with water, or watery melikraton.

beads.greek: τὸ δὲ ἀπὸ τῶν κοπρίων μηκώνειον ξυλλέγων ταμιεύου καὶ θεράπευε.
beads.english: And collect the mēkōneion that grows on the dung-heaps, store it, and treat with it.

Of scale, three probes' breadth, and of sētanion flour; having glued these together, ground them fine and rolled them into pills, give them; it purges water downwards and empties the bowel of faeces.

Onto dried figs drip juice of tithymallos, about seven times onto each, with the aforesaid; then, putting them together into a new vessel, store them, and give them to the aforesaid patient before food.
To the dropsical, grind the kōnion, pour water over it, and give it to eat and to drink after.

And grinding the mēkōneion, pouring water over it and straining it, kneading flour, baking a sesame cake, pouring boiled honey over it, give it to the dropsical to chew, and to drink after it sweet wine diluted with water, or watery melikraton.
And collect the mēkōneion that grows on the dung-heaps, store it, and treat with it.

beads.greek: [918] Φανερῶς ἐκ τῶν τοιούτων δηλοῦται τοῦτο τὸ βιβλίον ὑπόμνημα συμμίκτων εἶναι θεωρημάτων, ἀτάκτως τῆς μεταβάσεως ἀπ᾿ ἄλλων πρὸς ἄλλα γιγνομένης, ὥσπερ καὶ νῦν ἐπὶ τῆς ἐκ τῶν μυκτήρων αἱμοῤῥαγίας γέγραπται βοηθήματα, τὰ μὲν αὐτῷ τῷ μέρει τῷ αἱμοῤῥαγοῦντι προσφερόμενα, τὰ δὲ ἀντισπαστικὰ, καθάπερ ἡ γαστὴρ λυομένη, τὰ δὲ τῆς κεφαλῆς πυκνωτικὰ καὶ στυπτικὰ, καθάπερ τὰ ψύχοντα.
beads.english: [918] From passages such as these it is plainly shown that this book is a memorandum of miscellaneous doctrines (θεωρημάτων), the transition from some matters to others taking place without order. So too here, for haemorrhage from the nostrils, remedies have been written down: some applied to the bleeding part itself, others revulsive, as when the bowel is loosened, and others condensing and astringent of the head, as cooling things are.

beads.greek: τὰ δ᾿ ἐφεξῆς τούτων ἅπαντα φαρμάκων ἔχει γραφὰς καί τινα παραμεμιγμένα βοηθήματα.
beads.english: All that follows these contains prescriptions of drugs, with some remedies mixed in among them.

beads.greek: περὶ πρώτου μὲν οὖν τὸν λόγον ποιεῖται καλουμένου σησάμου, ἐφεξῆς δὲ τριχῶν ἐν τοῖς βλεφάροις χειρουργίαν ἔγραψεν, ἣν ὀνομάζουσιν ἀναβρογχισμόν.
beads.english: First he discusses what is called sesamon; next he wrote down the surgery for the hairs on the eyelids, which they call anabronchismos.

beads.greek: καὶ μετὰ ταῦτα πάλιν ὁμοίως αἱμοῤῥοΐδων καὶ τῆς ἄλλης ἰάσεως, εἶτ᾿ ἐμπύων φάρμακά τε καὶ ῥοφήματα καὶ μετὰ ταῦτα σκευασίας φαρμάκων ὀφθαλμικῶν.
beads.english: After this, again in the same way, he deals with haemorrhoids and the rest of their treatment; then drugs and gruels for empyemic patients; and after these, preparations of ophthalmic drugs.

First he discusses what is called sesamon; next he wrote down the surgery for the hairs on the eyelids, which they call anabronchismos.
After this, again in the same way, he deals with haemorrhoids and the rest of their treatment; then drugs and gruels for empyemic patients; and after these, preparations of ophthalmic drugs.

beads.greek: εἶτα περὶ τῶν ὑστερικῶν γινομένων, εἶτα περὶ τοῦ μηκωνείου, εἶθ᾿ ἑξῆς ὑδραγωγὸν φάρμακον, εἶτ᾿ ἐκκοπρωτικὸν, εἶθ᾿ ἑδρικοῖς, ὑδερικοῖς τε δίδωσι διὰ μηκωνείου καὶ [919] ἰτρίων.
beads.english: Then about what occurs in uterine affections, then about the mēkōnion (poppy juice), then next a hydragogue drug, then an evacuant of faeces, then for patients with complaints of the seat and for dropsical patients he gives a preparation made with mēkōnion and [919] itria (thin cakes).

beads.greek: ἔστιν οὖν ἐφεξῆς τῶν εἰρημένων τὰ μὲν πλεῖστα σαφῆ, παρέγκειται δέ τινα καὶ ἀσαφῆ, περὶ ὧν ἐφεξῆς ποιήσομαι τὸν λόγον.
beads.english: Of what follows the things already said, then, most is clear, but some unclear things have also been inserted alongside, and these I shall discuss next.
